newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-UMAGA POWERS HIS WAY INTO THE ALL BLACKS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-UMAGA POWERS HIS WAY INTO THE ALL BLACKS.

text.p: Powerful winger Tana Umaga was one of two new caps named in an otherwise predictable New Zealand All Black rugby team to play Fiji in a test match next Saturday.
Umaga, one of the outstanding players in the recent Super 12 competition, was given the nod on the left wing ahead of incumbent Glen Osborne, who has been relegated to the reserves bench.
Osborne originally replaced superstar Jonah Lomu, forced out of all rugby earlier this year by a kidney disorder and who is not expected back for several months yet.
Umaga represents the success story of the New Zealand rugby season so far, rising from just another provincial player to a Super 12 star and an All Black test player in barely three months.
The dreadlocked Wellington Hurricanes player has become a hero in that city, dazzling fans with his pace on the wing and powerful, puncturing runs in mid-field.
All Black coach John Hart said Umaga, 24, had adopted a professional attitude over the summer to gain fitness and that discipline had paid off.
The other newcomer to the test team is number eight Taine Randell, who is touted as a future All Black captain.

Randell is covering for the indomitable Zinzan Brooke, who was concussed during the Super 12 final between the Auckland Blues and Australia's ACT on May 31. Brooke is sure to return after the Fiji test.
Fiji coach Brad Johnstone conceded that the All Blacks posed a formidable challenge for his team in Saturday's test.
"We're up against the hottest international team in the world but we're there, and by virtue of that I guess we've got a chance," he said.
